bugs.title: A clean player revealed during an ad pod plays several seconds behind live and never closes the gap
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The clean player was only pulled onto the live edge when it was MORE than 20s behind AND only while an ad was active. A warm standby minted at page load sits wherever hls.js joined the live window (5-19s behind), so it passed the gate unchanged and was revealed one segment-delay behind the native. hls.js then plays at 1x and can never close a constant offset, so the delay was permanent for the whole pod. The user's own observation that dragging the bar forward a few seconds keeps working proves a forward seek inside the live window is safe, so the extension had no reason to leave the offset there. The same 20s gate also gated `healthy`, so a 12s-behind standby was considered fit to show.
bugs.falsifier: With a standby 12s behind the live edge, a reveal must hand the user a picture at the same offset as the native (within 3s of the edge). If the revealed player is left 12s behind, or is revealed without a seek, the fix did not take.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'quando troca o player porque ele protege de um ad, a live volta varios segundos'

Pre-fix code, kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js: frame-stats handler `if (overlay.adActive && typeof m.st.lat === 'number' && m.st.lat > 20) { ... seek to pos+lat-3 }` and `const latOk = ... || m.st.lat <= 20`. standby-start had its own 20s gate (`lat0 > 20`) and revealed without any catch-up below that

Fix (0.8.44): CLEAN_LAT_TARGET=3 / CLEAN_LAT_MAX=8 / RESUME_GAP_SEC=1.5, a single catchUpClean(st, force) helper shared by the frame-stats tick and by reveal, called for `overlay.adActive || overlay.standby`, plus a forced re-align at reveal when the standby is more than target+1.5s behind. cleanLatTarget() aims the clean player at the NATIVE's own offset captured at take-over (min 8, max 2 clamp) so the swap lands on the wall-clock second the user was watching

kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs drives the REAL kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js through the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs makePage/settle) and through the real ad path (ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal -> ad-end): `a standby 12s behind live is seeked onto the edge (not left there)` and `a 6s-behind standby is re-aligned before it covers the native`

Negative arm: restoring the pre-fix gate (`(overlay.adActive || overlay.standby)` -> `overlay.adActive && lat > 20`) makes the detector FAIL with the player left 12s behind, so the check measures the fix and not the harness
node kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS checks=13 failed=0
Gate: node _tools/ko-verify.mjs -> RESULT PASS checks=18 failed=0, new `ad-time-continuity` check
bugs.owner_validation: pending: installed 0.8.44 in his Chrome. Watch a pod, confirm the picture returns at real time (badge does not show a visibly late stream) and that dragging the bar back does not reveal a further delay.
bugs.next: Owner: with 0.8.44 installed, time the clean picture against the native edge on a real pod. Live pod not measured (no ad painted in the guest during the 2026-10-26 runs).

bugs.title: Ad-end jumps the picture: the native was seeked to its buffered end and resumed 300ms late through a lifecycle gate
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: resumeNative() seeked the native to `buffered.end - 0.5`, which is the newest frame the ELEMENT holds, not the offset the clean player was showing. On a native Twitch paused while it was covered that is a seek across the whole pod (a visible jump); on one that kept buffering it is a free jump forward past the clean position. Independently, ad-end called resumeNativeIfAllowed(), which refuses while `overlay.adActive` is still set and a revealed frame is still mounted - both true at that moment - so the hand-back was deferred to the 300ms retry, i.e. a frozen native frame followed by a jump.
bugs.falsifier: At ad-end the native must already stand at the offset the clean player had (edge - cleanLatTarget, within 1.5s), with no seek at all when it is already there. A hand-back that moves the native by seconds, or that leaves it frozen for a retry, is the defect.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'quando acaba o ad e o player volta, aí acontece um salto no tempo por causa disso'

Pre-fix code: `const be = v.buffered && v.buffered.length ? v.buffered.end(v.buffered.length - 1) : 0; if (be > v.currentTime + 3) { v.currentTime = be - 0.5 }` and ad-end `resumeNativeIfAllowed(v, 'now')` where that helper returns early on `overlay.adActive` / revealed frame

Fix (0.8.44): the hand-off seeks to `nativeEdge - cleanLatTarget()` (skip when the gap is under RESUME_GAP_SEC, log from/to/lat/gap), and ad-end resumes the native DIRECTLY under the user-intent guard only, so the frame and the picture change in the same tick

kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs drives the REAL kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js through the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs makePage/settle) and through the real ad path (ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal -> ad-end): `ad-end on a native already at the target offset does not seek` and `a native parked behind by the pod is handed back at edge-3`
Negative arm: restoring the buffered-end target makes the detector FAIL with ct=399.5 against a 397 target (a 2.5s jump), so the check is exercised
node kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS checks=13 failed=0
bugs.owner_validation: pending: installed 0.8.44. Watch an ad end while the native was covered for tens of seconds and confirm the picture continues instead of jumping.
bugs.next: Owner: confirm on a real pod end. The 300ms retry stays as a fallback for a native that Twitch unmounts mid-pod.

bugs.title: A mute change made during the swap is inverted: the extension reads its own write as the user's decision
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The user's mute decision was captured ONCE at take-over (adoptNativeMute/overlay.muteIntent) and never tracked afterwards, so an unmute during the pod reached the clean player only if the generic pointerdown handler fired - and that handler returned early for `overlay.muteIntent`, i.e. exactly the case of a user who had muted. The reverse direction came from the autoplay muting: the extension muted the clean frame to get it to play, and nothing marked that mute as OURS, so `autoplayMuted` was never set and the reveal treated the silence as the user's, while a page click later unmuted a user who had asked for silence.
bugs.falsifier: Unmute while the clean player covers the ad: the clean player must become audible immediately, and the ad-end hand-back must NOT re-mute the native. Mute, then click anywhere in the page: it must stay silent.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'eu desmutar rapidamente a live quando acontece o ad e troca de player, faz ele mutar o player. ou vice versa'

Pre-fix code: `document` pointerdown handler `if (!explicit && overlay.muteIntent) return;` (a muted user could never be unmuted by the flow that was supposed to unlock them) and reveal paths sending `mute: true` for autoplay with no flag distinguishing an autoplay mute from a user mute

Fix (0.8.44): a capture-phase `volumechange` listener (onNativeVolumeChange) tracks the user's decision continuously while the ad path owns playback, ignores our own writes within 400ms via noteMuteWrite(), forwards the decision to the revealed clean player immediately, and clears autoplayMuted on an explicit unmute. The pointerdown unlock now requires `overlay.autoplayMuted` before it may overrule silence

kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs drives the REAL kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js through the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs makePage/settle) and through the real ad path (ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal -> ad-end): `an unmute made during the pod reaches the clean player immediately` and `the in-pod unmute survives ad-end (the native is not re-muted)`
Negative arm: removing the volumechange listener (`void onNativeVolumeChange`) makes the detector FAIL on the in-pod unmute, so the check is exercised
node kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS checks=13 failed=0
bugs.owner_validation: pending: installed 0.8.44. Unmute mid-pod and confirm sound appears on the clean picture and stays on after the pod; mute and confirm a page click does not restore sound.
bugs.next: Owner: confirm both directions during a real pod. Recorder-only pages and hidden tabs never reach the handler (own guard).

bugs.title: The ad path unpauses a Twitch tab the user had paused, including one in a background tab
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: resumeNative() called play() on the native whenever the lifecycle allowed it, with no check on (a) document.visibilityState and (b) whether the user had paused the native before the pod. A tab left paused in the background is therefore started by the ad path as soon as a standby start or an ad-end tick reaches it, which is audible from another tab.
bugs.falsifier: A native that was already paused at take-over (and never played) must still be paused at ad-end, and a hidden tab must never be started. A cold preroll (paused at currentTime<1, i.e. the page just loaded) is the one case where starting it is correct.
evidence: Owner report 2026-11-07: 'tem vezes que estou em outra aba, com uma aba da twitch pausada, por algum motivo é despausado sozinho por causa da extensão'
Pre-fix code: resumeNative() had no visibility check and resumeNativeIfAllowed() only gated on the overlay lifecycle (`overlay.adActive`, revealed frame), never on the user's own pause

Fix (0.8.44): overlay.pauseBeforeAd / overlay.coldPreroll captured at take-over (both the ad-hold and the ad-start-without-hold paths) and a resumeRefusedByUser(v) guard - hidden tab, or a paused non-cold native - applied by resumeNativeIfAllowed and by the 1s watch tick and by ad-end

kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs drives the REAL kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js through the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs makePage/settle) and through the real ad path (ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal -> ad-end): `a player the user had paused is not restarted after the pod`, `a pod that ends while the tab is hidden never starts playback`, `a cold preroll still hands back a running player at edge-3`
Negative arm: emptying the guard body makes the detector FAIL (the paused native restarts), so the check is exercised
node kick-overlay/ad-time-continuity-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS checks=13 failed=0
bugs.owner_validation: pending: installed 0.8.44. Leave a Twitch tab paused in the background through an ad on another tab and confirm it stays paused.
bugs.next: Owner: confirm on a real background tab. A cold preroll keeps its own exception so the first paint after a page load still starts.

bugs.title: The stream keeps the previous channel after an SPA channel switch (revealed clean player is never stopped)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: Twitch changes channels with an SPA navigation: same document, same content-script instance, new location.pathname. The ad-free clean player is an overlay owned by that instance. The only channel checks in twitch-adblock.js were inside ad-hold/standby-start and they only applied while the overlay was an invisible STANDBY (`if (!overlay.standby) return` / `overlay.standby ? stop : cold path`). An overlay that was already revealed (a live ad pod) had no channel check and nothing in the module watched the route (no popstate/pushState/pathname poll), so after a switch the previous channel clean player stayed on screen, the native player stayed visibility:hidden/muted, and the next ad on the new channel also hit the early `overlay.frame && !overlay.standby` return. The user sees the previous streamer image and calls it "keeps the last stream".
bugs.falsifier: With a revealed clean player on channel A, changing location.pathname to channel B (the way Twitch does, no reload) must remove the A player and hand the native B player back instead of keeping the A stream attached.
evidence: Pre-fix code, kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js: ad-hold `if (overlay.frame && !overlay.standby) { ... return; }` had no channel comparison, and standby-start compared `overlay.channel` with `pageChannel()` only for a standby
Pre-fix code, same module: no route watcher at all (grep popstate|pushState|setInterval|pathname found only pageChannel() and the document_start standby requests)

kick-overlay/channel-switch-test.cjs runs the REAL twitch-adblock.js against the shared stubbed DOM (mute-decision-test.cjs), drives ad-hold -> ad-start -> ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks to a revealed overlay, then changes location.pathname like Twitch does. Pre-fix run (source before the fix), recorded output: `FAIL a revealed overlay of the previous channel is stopped on a channel switch`, `FAIL the native player is handed back after the switch  native still hidden (hidden)`, `FAIL an ad on the new channel cold-starts its own clean player  loads after the switch: ["https://clean.example/live.m3u8"]` — RESULT FAIL checks=9 failed=6

Fix (0.8.43): a 900 ms pathname watcher in the page module (same cadence as content.js SPA_MS). On a channel change it stops any overlay whose overlay.channel no longer matches pageChannel(); stopAdOverlay() restores the hidden videos, resumes the native player and posts overlay-stop so the worker clears adBypassActive and can retry on the new channel. Same-channel sub-routes (/ch/clips) do not trigger it

Post-fix: node kick-overlay/channel-switch-test.cjs -> RESULT PASS channel-switch checks=9 failed=0 (revealed dropped, native handed back, new ad cold-starts on the new channel, standby dropped, sub-route keeps the overlay, negative arm with the guard disabled still keeps the old player and native hidden)

Live arm, guest Chrome (port 9333), real module driven through its own BroadcastChannel protocol with a real minted clean master for twitch.tv/necros: standby-start -> Standby 0.01 / native visible, ad-hold -> overlay-reveal reason standby, adfix opacity 1, native visibility:hidden muted:true. Real click on the sidebar link to /aggeo (SPA): at the first 500 ms sample the A player was removed (adfix null), native visibility restored to visible and playing (ct 0 -> 3.6 s), and the new channel standby started at T+1s
Version 0.8.43; gate check `channel-switch` added to _tools/ko-verify.mjs
bugs.verified_by: lane, pre-fix RED + post-fix PASS through the real module (unit), plus a guest-Chrome SPA switch on live twitch.tv/necros -> /aggeo with a synthetic ad trigger through the shipped message protocol

bugs.title: Ad player swap unmutes a user who had muted (ignores the last mute decision)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The SSAI ad path covers Twitch with a separate clean hls.js frame that is started muted (Chrome autoplay). revealOverlay() then sent mute:false unconditionally. The native mute was captured (wasMuted/holdWasMuted) but only used to restore the native player at ad-end, so every pod handed sound back to a user who had muted. Two more paths broke the same decision: a warm standby minted at page load carried the mute state from load time (stale after a later mute), and the document-wide pointerdown handler unmuted on any click, including a click in chat. ad-end also restored wasMuted instead of the decision the user made during the pod (an explicit badge unmute was lost).
bugs.falsifier: On a real Twitch live with a user-muted native player, the clean ad frame starts playing audio, or a click outside the badge restores audio, or the native player comes back unmuted/muted against the user's last decision.
evidence: Owner report 2026-10-26: 'when i mute, the ad comes, player swaps, it unmutes. respect the last user decision.'

Pre-fix code, kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js revealOverlay(): `if (!overlay.unmuteTried) { overlay.unmuteTried = true; overlaySend({ t: 'mute', m: false }); ... }` with no read of wasMuted/holdWasMuted
Pre-fix code, stopAdOverlay(): `v.muted = overlay.wasMuted` — captured at pod start, so an in-pod unmute was reverted
Pre-fix code, unmuteHandler on document pointerdown: unmuted on ANY page click, regardless of the user's mute

kick-overlay/mute-decision-test.cjs runs the real twitch-adblock.js through ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal in a stubbed DOM: muted user gets no mute:false (and the badge offers click-to-sound), a generic page click does not unmute, a badge click does, ad-end restores the decision; an unmuted user still gets sound
Its negative arm replays the pre-fix gate (`if (overlay.muteIntent)` -> `if (false)`) and the muted scenario then DOES see mute:false, so the detector is exercised in both directions
Gate: node _tools/ko-verify.mjs -> RESULT PASS checks=12 failed=0, including the new mute-decision check

bugs.title: Black box over a YouTube watch page with player=kick (fixed in 0.8.42: `ready` was posted to the hardcoded twitch.tv origin)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: player-bridge.js posts `ready` to PARENT_ORIGIN, which is `https://www.twitch.tv` until a valid inbound message teaches the frame the real parent origin. On a youtube.com page the browser silently drops that post (targetOrigin mismatch), so the content script never sees `ready`, never hands over the pending playback_url, and the IVS player stays Idle until the 15s never-played watchdog tears the layer down. The origin is only learned when a kickSend lands AFTER the frame's load event (mute/volume/play from a later show), and `ready` is never re-posted, so the frame stays half-initialised for its whole life.
bugs.falsifier: CORRECTED by measurement (0.8.41). The pre-instrumentation falsifier ('KO.kickReady becomes true and the layer plays') is what the fix must satisfy; the measured falsifier for THIS cause is: a frame->page post with targetOrigin https://www.twitch.tv is actually delivered on a youtube.com page, or the frame reports `ready` accepted by the content script while `parentLearnedAt` is still 0.
evidence: Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jfKfPfyJRdk, ko.v2 player=kick, mapping rodil -> {kick: rodil, yt: that video}
Guest Chrome 2026-10-26 (0.8.41 instrumentation), frame token d20935ab matched on BOTH sides (page KO.kickFrame.dataset.koToken === frame __koBridgeDiag.token)
Frame side, before any inbound message: posts.ready=1 at ms=684 with to='https://www.twitch.tv', learned=false; posts.st=7 also to twitch.tv; parentLearnedAt=0; inbound.total=0
Page side, same moment: KO.kickDiag.accepted=0, drops={} (nothing was dropped by the page guards), KO.kickReady=false, KO.pendingUrl=true

Primitive check, same frame: frame->page postMessage with targetOrigin 'https://www.twitch.tv' delivered 0 times (parent is youtube.com); page->frame with '*' delivered, and with the extension origin delivered

Causal arm: one valid inbound getState from the page -> frame parentLearnedAt=8432ms, learnedFrom={origin:'https://www.youtube.com', fromParent:true}, inbound={total:1,accepted:1}; the page then accepts st immediately (accepted 0 -> 2, byType {st:2}, firstAt.st=9393). ready is still never accepted (readyFrame=null): it was posted once, at 684ms, before the origin was known

Explains the earlier run in this ticket: st only started arriving at 21.4s, right after the first successful kickSend (mute/volume/play at 21.2s, sentByType {mute,volume,play}); before that showKickLayer's sends were blocked (KO.kickDiag.blockedSend=4) because KO.kickWin is only set on the frame's load event

bugs.title: The hand-back trusted Twitch's 2^30 seekable end as a live edge and seeked the native a billion seconds forward
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: nativeEdge() returned seekable.end for a live element, and Twitch reports 1073741824 (2^30) as a 'live, timeline unknown' sentinel. cleanLatTarget() then clamped it to 8 and resumeNative() computed `se - cleanLatTarget()` = 1073741816, which is a seek far past the end of any stream.
